transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-06
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Marcus Chen (Avalon CTO), Sofia Alvarez (Avalon SRE Lead), Liam O'Neil (Avalon PM)

Summary (auto): Discovery of reliability and incident tolerance needs; discussed multi-region routing, model fallbacks, SLA expectations, and security requirements. Agreed on follow-ups: pricing/SLA docs, technical deep-dive, and traffic export for benchmarks.

Topics: reliability, multi-region, fallbacks, dedicated vs hosted, private deployment, SLA, KMS, SSO, audit logs, caching, batching

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood. How's it going?
[00:04] Marcus: Good thanks. Marcus here, CTO. We try to keep this short, we've got about 40 minutes.
[00:08] Jordan: Sounds good. Priya from our solutions engineering team is with me, she'll take the deep technical questions.
[00:12] Priya: Hi all, nice to meet you.
[00:14] Sofia: Hi, Sofia here. I'll be focused on SRE requirements and incident response.
[00:17] Liam: Liam, product. We're evaluating options for hosted vs dedicated since we have compliance and latency needs.
[00:22] Jordan: Great, why don't we start with your current setup and what "must-haves" look like. Marcus, maybe you can kick us off?
[00:29] Marcus: Sure. Right now we're on a mix: internal services call OpenAI via hosted keys for prototyping, and some self-hosted models for inference-heavy flows. Our core user-facing chat path needs p95 under 300ms ideally 200ms, esp in US and EU. We have around 1k rps at peak globally with spikes to 2.5k, it's... "spiky".
[00:45] Priya: 1k to 2.5k peak, got it. Are those synchronous user requests or async batching?
[00:49] Marcus: Mostly sync, user-facing. We can tolerate small tail latency but not timeouts at the front-end.
[00:54] Sofia: And from SRE side we need predictable failover. If an instance or AZ goes down we need automatic reroute to warm capacity in a different region within 15s ideally.
[01:03] Jordan: That's a helpful constraint. We do multi-region routing and can configure routing policies by latency or by region + tier. One question — are you leaning Hosted API, Redwood Dedicated, or Private?
[01:13] Liam: From product, we'd prefer Hosted for speed of launch, but we have security and residency requirements for some markets that push us toward Dedicated or Private. Cost is also a factor.
[01:22] Marcus: Also, in incidents we want graceful degradation — fallback to smaller models or cached responses rather than failing entirely.
[01:29] Priya: Right. So we typically recommend a hybrid approach: Hosted for prototypes and non-sensitive traffic, Dedicated for production workloads where you need reserved capacity and SLAs, Private when you need full network isolation or on-prem. You can also set policy-based routing so requests fail over to a cheaper/less precise model when your primary capacity is constrained.
[01:46] Marcus: Do you support automatic fallbacks? For example, if the nv-1 pool is saturated, can requests route to nv-2 in a different region automatically?
[01:54] Priya: Yes. We have smart routing + fallback chains. You can define primary model/region, then a sequence of compatible model variants and regions. In practice we've seen setups where the primary is a large LLM in US-West and fallback is a quantized variant in US-East, or a lower-cost hosted model. There is a small added latency when cross-region, but it avoids complete failures.
[02:13] Sofia: How do you handle KV cache and prefix caching across regions? If we route to another region, we'd lose warm KV cache and that could spike latency.
[02:21] Priya: Great point. We support both local KV caching and a shared cache option. Shared cache adds network overhead but keeps hits across regions; local caches warm per-region and you can set TTLs. Usually for tight p95 targets you'd want local warm caches plus pre-warming strategies during failover.
[02:36] Marcus: What's the expected SLA for Dedicated? We need numbers for uptime and latency SLOs to present to execs.
[02:44] Jordan: Our Dedicated product comes with an SLA on availability — typically 99.95% for capacity-backed contracts; we can share the exact legal wording in the SLA doc. For latency SLOs, we do per-route percentiles and tooling to measure — but contractual latency SLOs are something we can discuss on a case basis.
[03:00] Sofia: Do you do regional capacity reservations? Meaning if US-East goes down do we have guaranteed reserved warm nodes in US-West?
[03:08] Priya: Reserved capacity is per-pool and can be pinned to regions. You can purchase burst capacity in secondary regions, or configure warm standby nodes. It's a tradeoff on cost.
[03:17] Liam: Cost question — how much overhead for multi-region standby? Ballpark.
[03:21] Jordan: It depends on commit level; typical architectures reserve 20-30% standby capacity cross-region; we can model numbers if you share traffic profiles.
[03:30] Marcus: We'll share the profiles. Another thing: incident response. Do you provide automatic rollback to older model versions if a new deployment regresses?
[03:39] Priya: Yes, we have rollout controls: canary, A/B, and automatic fallback to previous pinned versions if errors or quality regressions cross thresholds. Also tracing and per-token cost breakdown to help root cause.
[03:50] Sofia: Audit logs and encryption — we need KMS integration and full auditability for access. Also SSO/SAML for RBAC.
[03:59] Jordan: We support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, HSM options for Private) and audit logs shipped to your SIEM. SSO/SAML with SCIM provisioning and role-based policies are supported.
[04:12] Marcus: Any SOC2 or ISO attestations? For our procurement team.
[04:15] Jordan: We have SOC2 Type II. We'll attach certs in the follow-up.
[04:18] Liam: On the performance side, have you benchmarked p95 for token streaming across regions? We're sensitive to end-to-end latency including network.
[04:26] Priya: We have public benchmarks and internal profiles; for streaming p95 within a region we've seen sub-200ms on optimized GPU instances for many model families, but cross-region adds network RTT. We can run a benchmark with your traffic pattern — that’s why we asked for sample traffic.
[04:39] Marcus: Okay. Also how do you handle degradation in quality when falling back to smaller models? We can't have hallucinations in some flows.
[04:46] Priya: You can define quality gates per route — for some routes we allow only model family fallbacks whereas for others we can serve cached or templated responses. Redwood Optimize can also recommend which model quantizations are safe for a given workload.
[04:58] Sofia: From SRE, we need the failover time numbers and runbooks. Do you provide runbooks and playbooks for integrated incidents?
[05:05] Jordan: Yes, customers get runbooks and recommendations; for Dedicated/Private we do runbook workshops as part of onboarding.
[05:12] Marcus: Practical question — if we choose Hosted for the first phase, how hard is it to move to Dedicated later? Migration effort?
[05:20] Priya: The API and routing config is consistent across modes. Migration is mostly an infra/config change — pinning to dedicated model versions and updating routing policies — but there are some network config and credential changes. We have migration templates.
[05:32] Liam: Any limits on model families? We use a custom fine-tuned LLM for some flows.
[05:36] Priya: We can onboard custom models for Dedicated and Private — with Hosted it's more limited but we do support bringing your own model to Dedicated. There is a model validation step for performance and compatibility.
[05:46] Marcus: And for private deployments, can we run in our VPC with no egress to the public internet?
[05:52] Jordan: Yes, Private can be deployed in your VPC with customer-managed control plane, and we have on-prem variants for air-gapped environments.
[05:59] Sofia: How about monitoring integration? Prometheus, Grafana, Datadog?
[06:03] Priya: We export metrics to Prometheus, logs to your ingestion (e.g., Datadog); dashboards are available in Redwood Console.
[06:10] Marcus: Ok, some specifics on fallback policies. Suppose model A in us-west has errors; what are typical routing chains and what latency impact should we plan for?
[06:19] Priya: Typical chain: primary large model in region A -> pinned quantized variant in same region -> replicate fallback in secondary region -> hosted cheap model as last resort. Cross-region fallback adds RTT; if your p95 target is 200ms, cross-region fallback will likely push you beyond target, so pre-warmed standby and local quantized variants are recommended.
[06:39] Liam: Can we set per-route thresholds that trigger fallback, like error rate > 2% or latency > 95th baseline?
[06:46] Priya: Yes, you can set triggers based on error rates, latency, or specific response checks. We also support synthetic probing for health checks.
[06:55] Marcus: What about cost reporting during incidents? We need transparency on token costs when fallback to hosted increases spend.
[07:03] Jordan: Redwood Console shows token-level cost breakdowns and per-route cost spikes. We'll include that in the pricing discussion.
[07:10] Sofia: For culture and ops, will our SREs be able to trigger an emergency failover manually?
[07:15] Priya: Yes — manual controls are available and you can have RBAC so only authorized users can change routing or take capacity actions.
[07:22] Marcus: Anything we should be aware of for GDPR/data residency when routing between regions?
[07:27] Jordan: You can configure routing policies to respect data residency constraints and restrict models/regions for certain routes. Also Dedicated/Private gives more control over data residency.
[07:36] Liam: One more: what's the expected RTO for a regional outage? I'm hearing warm standby within 15s, but what's realistic?
[07:43] Priya: If you have pre-warmed standby and local caches, failover can be within 10-20s for routing; warming models and KV cache may take longer if not pre-warmed. That's why we recommend a small set of pre-warmed instances in secondary regions for critical routes.
[07:58] Marcus: Do you do automated canary analysis to detect quality regressions that should trigger rollback?
[08:03] Priya: Yes — we support canary metrics, regen tests, and threshold-based automatic rollback.
[08:08] Sofia: On encryption, are request/response tokens encrypted at rest and in transit with customer keys?
[08:14] Jordan: In transit always encrypted; at rest we support customer-managed KMS for Dedicated/Private. Hosted uses our KMS by default but we can add options for BYOK under contract.
[08:24] Marcus: Great. Let's talk about concrete next steps: we want pricing/SLA and a technical deep-dive. Also we'll provide traffic profiles.
[08:32] Jordan: Perfect. We'll send the Dedicated pricing + SLA and a benchmark workbook. Priya will schedule the deep-dive.
[08:38] Liam: For the technical deep dive, can we include a simulated failover test with your team?
[08:42] Priya: Absolutely — we can run a scheduled failover drill in staging to measure cold/warm failover and cache behavior.
[08:49] Marcus: Ok good. A couple of small notes: procurement will need SOC2 and compliance docs, and our security team will run a questionnaire.
[08:57] Jordan: We'll attach SOC2 certs and a security package; I'll also include contact for our compliance engineer.
[09:03] Sofia: Also please include recommended pre-warm counts and estimated cost impact for us to review.
[09:08] Jordan: We'll model that once you share traffic profile.
[09:11] Liam: Anything else from Redwood you want to surface?
[09:14] Priya: Just one note: Redwood Optimize can analyze your traffic and recommend quantization profiles and batching settings to hit latency/cost targets with minimal quality loss. We'll include sample reports.
[09:27] Marcus: Sounds good.
[09:29] Jordan: Quick clarification — for fallbacks, if you want deterministic non-hallucinated responses we can suggest templated fallback content for some routes rather than model fallbacks.
[09:40] Sofia: Good idea.
[09:42] Liam: Ok let's recap.
[09:44] Jordan: Recap: Jordan will send pricing + SLA + SOC2 and compliance pack. Priya will schedule technical deep dive and share multi-region configs and benchmark notes. Avalon to send 7-day traffic export and identify 2-3 critical routes to test failover. We'll plan a staged failover drill.
[10:02] Marcus: Yep that's right. Thanks everyone.
[10:05] Jordan: Thanks, we'll follow up with the docs.
[10:07] (call ends)

References shared in call: Pricing deck link (internal): https://redwood.example.com/decks/dedicated-pricing.pdf ; Benchmark workbook (note): shared after call via email; Security pack: /attachments/security-soc2.pdf
